punchline: A filtered chicken tumor, dismissed in 1911, won a Nobel Prize 55 years later.
thirty_sec: In 1911 Peyton Rous showed that a cell-free filtrate from a chicken sarcoma could give tumors to other fowl, the Rous sarcoma virus. The idea was dismissed at first; he shared the 1966 Nobel Prize with Charles Huggins at age 87.
question: Which well-founded idea have you dropped only because others were not ready?
key_contrast: A correct result and a world that took 55 years to catch up.
